In [[model theory]], a discipline within the field of [[mathematical logic]], a '''tame abstract elementary class''' is an [[abstract elementary class]] (AEC) which satisfies a locality property for types called tameness. Even though it appears implicitly in earlier work of [[Saharon Shelah|Shelah]], tameness as a property of AEC was first isolated by [[Rami Grossberg|Grossberg]] and VanDieren,<ref>{{harvnb|Grossberg|VanDieren|2006a}}.</ref> who observed that tame AECs were much easier to handle than general AECs.

== Definition ==

Let ''K'' be an [[abstract elementary class|AEC]] with joint embedding, amalgamation, and no maximal models. Just like in first-order model theory, this implies ''K'' has a universal model-homogeneous monster model <math>\mathfrak{C}</math>. Working inside <math>\mathfrak{C}</math>, we can define a semantic notion of [[type (model theory)|types]] by specifying that two elements ''a'' and ''b'' have the same type over some base model <math>M</math> if there is an [[automorphism]] of the monster model sending ''a'' to ''b'' fixing <math>M</math> pointwise (note that types can be defined in a similar manner without using a monster model<ref>{{harvnb|Shelah|2009}}, Definition II.1.9.</ref>). Such types are called '''Galois types'''.

One can ask for such types to be determined by their restriction on a small domain. This gives rise to the notion of tameness:

* An AEC <math>K</math> is ''tame'' if there exists a cardinal <math>\kappa</math> such that any two distinct Galois types are already distinct on a submodel of their domain of size <math>\le \kappa</math>. When we want to emphasize <math>\kappa</math>, we say <math>K</math> is <math>\kappa</math>-tame.

Tame AECs are usually also assumed to satisfy amalgamation.

== Discussion and motivation ==

While (without the existence of [[large cardinal]]s) there are examples of non-tame AECs,<ref>{{harvnb|Baldwin|Shelah|2008}}.</ref> most of the known natural examples are tame.<ref>See the discussion in the introduction of {{harvnb|Grossberg|VanDieren|2006a}}.</ref> In addition, the following sufficient conditions for a class to be tame are known:

* '''Tameness is a large cardinal axiom''':<ref>{{harvnb|Boney|2014}}, Theorem 1.3.</ref> There are class-many almost [[strongly compact cardinal]]s if and only if any abstract elementary class is tame.
* '''Some tameness follows from categoricity''':<ref>{{harvnb|Shelah|1999}}, Main claim 2.3 (9.2 in the online version).</ref> If an AEC with amalgamation is categorical in a cardinal <math>\lambda</math> of high-enough cofinality, then tameness holds for types over saturated models of size less than <math>\lambda</math>.
* '''Conjecture 1.5 in <ref>{{harvnb|Grossberg|VanDieren|2006b}}.</ref>''':   If K is categorical in some λ ≥ Hanf(K) then there exists χ < Hanf(K) such that K is χ-tame.

Many results in the model theory of (general) AECs assume weak forms of the [[Generalized continuum hypothesis]] and rely on sophisticated combinatorial set-theoretic arguments.<ref>See for example many of the hard theorems of Shelah's book ({{harvnb|Shelah|2009}}).</ref> On the other hand, the model theory of tame AECs is much easier to develop, as evidenced by the results presented below.

== Results ==

The following are some important results about tame AECs.

* '''Upward categoricity transfer''':<ref>{{harvnb|Grossberg|VanDieren|2006b}}.</ref> A <math>\kappa</math>-tame AEC with amalgamation that is categorical in some [[successor cardinal|successor]] <math>\lambda \ge \operatorname{LS}(K)^{++} + \kappa^+</math> (i.e. has exactly one model of size <math>\lambda</math> up to isomorphism) is categorical in ''all'' <math>\mu \ge \lambda</math>.
* '''Upward stability transfer''':<ref>See {{harvnb|Baldwin|Kueker|VanDieren|2006}}, Theorem 4.5 for the first result and {{harvnb|Grossberg|VanDieren|2006a}} for the second.</ref> A <math>\kappa</math>-tame AEC with amalgamation that is [[stable]] in a cardinal <math>\lambda \ge \kappa</math> is stable in <math>\lambda^+</math> and in every infinite <math>\mu</math> such that <math>\mu^\lambda = \mu</math>.
* '''Tameness can be seen as a topological separation principle''':<ref>{{harvnb|Lieberman|2011}}, Proposition 4.1.</ref> An AEC with amalgamation is tame if and only if an appropriate [[Topological space|topology]] on the set of Galois types is [[Hausdorff space|Hausdorff]].
* '''Tameness and categoricity imply there is a forking notion''':<ref>See {{harvnb|Vasey|2014}} for the first result, and {{harvnb|Boney|Vasey|2014}}, Corollary 6.10.5 for the result on dimension.</ref> A <math>\kappa</math>-tame AEC with amalgamation that is categorical in a cardinal <math>\lambda</math> of [[cofinality]] greater than or equal to <math>\kappa</math> has a good frame: a forking-like notion for types of singletons (in particular, it is [[stable]] in all cardinals). This gives rise to a well-behaved notion of [[dimension]].
